title: Objectwise injective-resolution cohomology comparison
statement: For an injective resolution I of F, there are objectwise isomorphisms from the homology of the evaluated complex to the cohomology presheaf, compatible with every restriction morphism.

proof.text: For an arbitrary injective resolution, construct the contravariant functor of degreewise additive Hom complexes. Extend from natural to integer degrees by zero, using mapExtendIso and extendHomologyIso. Identify it with the from-single Hom complex using Cochain.fromSingleEquiv; leftHomologyData identifies its homology with cohomology classes, and extAddEquivCohomologyClass identifies these with Ext.

Prove naturality in the first Hom argument. The from-single complex isomorphism commutes with precomposition. Represent every cocycle by fromSingleMk and apply mk₀_comp_extMk to prove compatibility of the Ext comparison. Construct LeftHomologyMapData for precomposition and combine its homologyMap_eq with the extension and complex naturality squares.

Represent sections by the free abelian sheaf on a representable: compose sheafificationAdjunction.homAddEquiv, the whiskered free-abelian adjunction, and yonedaEquiv. Prove its naturality in both the sheaf argument (postcomposition) and the site object (restriction). Apply it degreewise to construct a natural isomorphism of the evaluated resolution and its representing Hom complexes.

Because the site object universe and coefficient universe are independent, lift both complex functors into their common universe. The fully faithful additive universe-lift functors preserve homology; use ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality to transport the complex comparison to homology, then compose with the natural Ext comparison.

Cancel the common fully faithful lift functor using Functor.fullyFaithfulCancelRight. Take the components of the resulting natural isomorphism as the requested objectwise isomorphisms; its naturality is exactly the stated restriction compatibility.

proof_origin.place: Step 2; explicit Lean construction using the free-sheaf adjunction and injective-resolution Ext computation
